text:
**Short answer:** for most tent or car campers, a 250-500Wh LiFePO4 unit is the best pick. It's light enough to carry one-handed and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP. If you need a fridge or multi-day power, step up to 1,000Wh or more.

## Compact picks (weekend trips)

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W AC): PowerStationGearLab's [top camping pick](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Jackery has since replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you may find the Plus mainly at third-party retailers.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC): [best value in that guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). It has double the Jackery's output and expands to 572Wh.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty): the cheapest 288Wh option per the [same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Make sure you buy the version with an AC outlet, not the "C300 DC." OutdoorGearLab's [lab testing](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) scored the C300 lower (50/100) than larger units, so it suits light use best.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC): the budget choice, per the [same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).

## Bigger picks (fridge, multi-day, van/overland)

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (39 lb, 2,200W): OutdoorGearLab's [best for off-grid camping](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station). It was under $900 on Amazon at the time of their update (list price $1,499).
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (25 lb): OutdoorGearLab's [best value](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station), on sale for under $530. The fan is noisy.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (1,536Wh, IP65, ~40 lb): WIRED's [best for camping](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/), at $1,079-$1,199.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, ~23.8 lb): the van pick in the [PowerStationGearLab guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), and [TechRadar's camping pick](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations).
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, 5-year warranty): a mid-size option for weekend trips and power tools. It's $499, or **$474.05 with code AFF5OFF**, which the listing says it tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy at Bluetti (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). It has no expansion port, and the store's checkout has the final word on price.

## Quick sizing

- Phones, lights, and a camera need about 288Wh.
- A CPAP uses roughly 30-60Wh a night with the humidifier off.
- A fridge for a few days is where you need 1,000Wh or more.
- For solar recharging, pair the unit with a panel from the same brand.

I only have retailer links for the Bluetti AC180. For the other models, the review pages above have the "check price" buttons, and prices change often, so confirm before you buy.

If you tell me what you plan to run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
